title: Recommendation ITU-R BS.1770-5: Algorithms to measure audio programme loudness and true-peak audio level
key_findings: Current in-force version approved 2023-11; defines programme loudness (LKFS = LUFS) and true-peak measurement.
Annex 2 gives guidelines for accurate true-peak measurement (oversampling) because sample peaks miss inter-sample overs.
It is the measurement basis cited by EBU R128, Spotify, Apple Podcasts.
practical_applications: Every loudness number in our pipeline (ffmpeg ebur128/loudnorm) should be BS.1770 based so platform figures are comparable.
limitations: Only the ITU product page and search snippets were read; Annex details not checked.

title: EBU R 128 (2020, v4.0): Loudness normalisation and permitted maximum level of audio signals
key_findings: Normalise to Programme Loudness; Target Level -23.0 LUFS, tolerance +/-1.0 LU where target not practically achievable (live).
Measure the whole programme, not only speech or music (no 'anchor' emphasis); gated measurement per BS.1770 eq. 7.
Maximum True Peak -1 dBTP in production; lower limits may apply for distribution systems / data reduction (see EBU Tech 3344).
Loudness Range (Tech 3342), max momentary and max short-term loudness are descriptors, not targets.
practical_applications: Use -23 LUFS only for broadcast deliveries; social video uses streaming targets but the same metering method.
Keep TP <= -1 dBTP as an absolute ceiling; lower before lossy encoding.
limitations: Broadcast standard, not a social-platform spec. A 2023 v5.0 exists (seen in search, not read).

title: Loudness normalization on Spotify (Spotify for Artists support)
key_findings: Default playback target -14 LUFS (ITU 1770); user modes Loud -11, Normal -14, Quiet -19 LUFS.
Positive gain is capped by the track's peak with 1 dB headroom for lossy encoding; loud mode uses a limiter (-1 dB, 5 ms attack, 100 ms release).
Advice: master to about -14 LUFS, keep true peak below -1 dBTP; if louder than -14 LUFS keep below -2 dBTP.
No normalization on the web player and some third-party devices.
practical_applications: Good reference for 'loud masters get turned down, quiet masters may not be fully raised' logic that also applies to video platforms.
limitations: Music-streaming platform, not a video platform. Undated support page; values can change.

title: Apple Podcasts for Creators: Audio requirements
key_findings: Target around -16 LKFS +/-1 dB, true peak not above -1 dBFS, both per ITU-R BS.1770-5; condition loudness before encoding.
WAV/FLAC min 44.1 kHz, 16- or 24-bit; 24-bit recommended; mono masters must be delivered as dual-mono stereo for WAV/FLAC.
practical_applications: Use -16 LUFS for speech-only audio deliverables (podcast-style VO, audio-only posts).
limitations: Podcast spec; not a video-platform rule.

title: AES TD1008: Recommendations for loudness of internet audio streaming and on-demand distribution (republished as AES77-2023)
authors: Audio Engineering Society Technical Committee on Broadcast and Online Delivery
key_findings: Guidance for distributors (not producers) on distribution loudness for music streams, radio-style streams and podcasts; supersedes TD1004.
Per Shepherd's summary: music -16 LUFS distribution loudness (album/loudest-track at ~-14), speech-only and assorted content -18 LUFS.
practical_applications: Explains why platform targets cluster at -14 to -18 LUFS and why speech-only content is often played quieter than music.
limitations: Numbers taken from a practitioner summary (ProductionAdvice), not read in the AES document itself.

title: AES TD1008 summary (ProductionAdvice)
key_findings: Summarises TD1008: music -16 LUFS; speech/podcast/'assorted' -18 LUFS; interstitials and assistant audio -18 LUFS.
practical_applications: Secondary reference for speech-only targets.
limitations: Practitioner summary; no true-peak figure stated in the summary.

title: Are you confused about exactly what YouTube's playback volume normalization is doing to your music?
key_findings: YouTube 'Stats for nerds' shows 'content loudness' = difference between a video's loudness and YouTube's reference.
YouTube only turns loud videos down; quieter videos are not turned up.
practical_applications: Check an uploaded clip: right-click > Stats for nerds; positive content loudness means YouTube is attenuating it.
limitations: 2017 article; YouTube publishes no official loudness target (no Google help page found this session). The often-quoted -14 LUFS reference is practitioner-reported (e.g. MeterPlugs 2019).

title: How Meta brought high-quality audio to Facebook and Instagram with the xHE-AAC codec
key_findings: xHE-AAC with MPEG-D DRC deployed for Facebook and Instagram Reels/Stories: loudness metadata, original audio untouched, client applies a context-dependent target loudness and DRC (headphones, speaker, noise).
No target LUFS value is published.
practical_applications: On Reels/Stories the final playback loudness is decided by the app; deliver a consistent, well-limited master and do not rely on extreme loudness.
limitations: Engineering blog, not a spec; no numbers.

title: LUFS targets per platform 2026
key_findings: Lists TikTok / Instagram / Meta as having no published loudness target (approx. -14 internal, context-adaptive), -1 dBTP advised.
practical_applications: Supports our position: for TikTok/IG use a sensible default, not a 'required' number.
limitations: Vendor blog; snippets only; internal values are estimates.

title: Preferred levels for background ducking to produce esthetically pleasing audio for TV with clear speech
authors: Torcoli, M.; Freke-Morin, A.; Paulus, J.; Simon, C.; Shirley, B.
key_findings: J. Audio Eng. Soc. 67(12) 2019: for a pleasant mix with clear speech, recommends at least 10 LU between commentary and music, and at least 15 LU between commentary and ambience; non-experts preferred about 4 LU more than experts.
Recommendation: at least 10 LU between commentary and music, at least 15 LU between commentary and ambience.
Non-experts preferred LDs about 4 LU higher than experts (significant); preferences varied widely between listeners.
Earlier convention version: listeners over 50 preferred at least 7 LU (under 50 no clear preference).
practical_applications: Core number for our VO mix: music bed >= 10 LU below VO while speaking, ambience >= 15 LU below; we are 'experts' so err louder VO than we like.
limitations: 22 listeners, normal hearing, TV documentary material, German lab; LD measured on short items.
Spot-check 2026-11-25: target is preference with clear speech; venue JAES.

title: [exact title not confirmed] JAES review of object-based audio personalisation for hard-of-hearing listeners
key_findings: Systematic review: spatial separation, speech-to-noise ratio and redundancy are evidenced to improve intelligibility; no single solution fits all hearing-impaired listeners.
practical_applications: Use all three levers in VO mixes: level difference, keep music out of the VO's centre/frequency space, redundancy (on-screen text = subtitles).
limitations: Exact title not confirmed; JAES vol. 67 pp. 584-597 per search snippets; content read only from snippets.

title: ISO 226:2023 Acoustics - Normal equal-loudness-level contours
key_findings: Third edition (2023): equal-loudness contours for pure tones 20 Hz-12.5 kHz, otologically normal listeners aged 18-25.
practical_applications: Explains why bass and very high treble sound quieter at low playback levels -> mixes checked only loud sound thin when quiet on a phone.
limitations: Standard not read; product page/snippets only.

title: [exact title not confirmed] Review of the ISO 226:2023 revision (Acoustical Science and Technology 45(1) 1-8)
authors: Suzuki, Y.; Takeshima, H.; Kurakata, K.
key_findings: 2023 revision differs from 2003 by at most 0.6 dB; motivated by a 0.4 dB lower threshold at 20 Hz (ISO 389-7:2019) and an updated loudness exponent.
practical_applications: The 2003 curves remain fine for mixing intuition.
limitations: Title paraphrased from search result; snippets only.

title: An Introduction to the Psychology of Hearing (6th ed.)
key_findings: Ch.3 'Frequency selectivity, masking and the critical band': auditory filters, power-spectrum model of masking.
Masking spreads more upward in frequency than downward; critical bandwidth grows with centre frequency.
practical_applications: Why a bass-heavy or mid-heavy music bed masks VO consonants more than its level suggests; carve the music where the VO lives.
limitations: Only table of contents / search snippets read.

title: Digital dynamic range compressor design - a tutorial and analysis
authors: Giannoulis, D.; Massberg, M.; Reiss, J. D.
key_findings: Compressors are nonlinear systems with memory; compares peak vs RMS detection, feed-forward vs feedback; recommends feed-forward designs as stable and predictable.
practical_applications: Explains threshold / ratio / knee / attack / release used in our acompressor settings.
limitations: Abstract only. JAES 60(6) 399-408.

title: 0 dBFS+ levels in digital mastering
key_findings: Inter-sample peaks can be considerably higher than 0 dBFS; consumer CD players reproduce such signals with distortion.
practical_applications: Reason to meter true peak (dBTP), not sample peak, and to leave >= 1 dB headroom before AAC encoding.
limitations: AES convention paper, abstract only.

title: FFmpeg Filters Documentation (loudnorm, ebur128, sidechaincompress, acompressor, afftdn, agate, deesser, alimiter)
key_findings: loudnorm: EBU R128 normalisation with dynamic and linear modes; single pass and two pass; defaults I=-24, LRA=7, TP=-2; dynamic mode upsamples to 192 kHz so set -ar explicitly.
linear=true needs all measured_* values; reverts to dynamic if target LRA < source LRA or the gain would exceed target TP.
acompressor/sidechaincompress defaults: threshold 0.125, ratio 2, attack 20 ms, release 250 ms; afftdn default nr 12 dB, nf -50 dB.
practical_applications: All command examples in MIX_PLAYBOOK.md were run on ffmpeg 9.0 (gyan.dev build) on synthetic audio this session.
limitations: In our test, loudnorm pass-1 input_i differed from ebur128 by about 0.9 LU on a synthetic signal - always re-measure the output.

title: Managing sibilance / Vocal de-essing (Sound On Sound techniques)
key_findings: Offending sibilance usually 5-8 kHz (SOS review); many vocal mics have a presence boost around 5 kHz; over-de-essing dulls the voice.
practical_applications: De-esser band for Thai/English TTS: start 5-8 kHz, then listen.
limitations: Snippets only; craft advice.

title: Digitizing audio (EECS 4462 course notes)
key_findings: Sampling theorem: sample rate must exceed twice the highest frequency; bit depth sets quantisation noise floor ~6.02 dB per bit (+1.76 dB for a full-scale sine), 16-bit ~ 96 dB.
practical_applications: 48 kHz / 24-bit (or 32-bit float) for production files; 16-bit is fine for final delivery.
limitations: Read via search snippets only.

title: GSMArena labs: smartphone loudspeaker test methodology
key_findings: Measures phone speaker frequency response with a sweep and reports loudness in LUFS; shows strong bass roll-off on phone speakers.
practical_applications: Motivation for a phone-speaker check (high-pass ~150 Hz preview) in QC.
limitations: No published cut-off numbers in what we saw; consumer-review methodology.
